description:
Research Summary

The University of Surrey is offering a doctorate on AI-assisted camera-lens design.

The project combines computer vision, graphics and computational imaging to connect optical design choices with image quality.

Official Project Title

Smart optical design: AI tools for the next generation of cinematic camera lenses

Research Focus and Methods

Develop differentiable, data-driven models for forward imaging simulation and inverse lens design. Investigate ways to propose lens architectures that meet imaging or perceptual objectives.

Research Training and Development

Research connects AI methods with industrial optical-design problems.

Funding and Duration

Studentship funding and award conditions
ComponentDetails
AwardPhD studentship; selection is competitive
ProgrammeSurrey studentship
Duration42 months (3.5 years)
Stipend£21,805 per year at the advertised 2026/27 UKRI rate; later rates follow the award terms.
Tuition and research supportHome fees or an international-fee waiver, stipend, research training and travel funds.
Award conditionsSelection is competitive; an advertised project does not guarantee a studentship.
Stipend amount status£21,805 is the published 2026/27 reference rate. Subsequent academic-year rates and the amount in an individual funding offer should be checked separately.

Eligibility and English Language

Applicant qualifications and funding eligibility
ComponentDetails
Applicant eligibilityWorldwide applicants may apply, subject to programme and university requirements.
Academic preparationFirst-class or high 2:1 honours degree or equivalent in computer science, electronic engineering, applied mathematics, physics or a related subject; a relevant master’s is preferred.
Project interests and skillsStrong mathematics and Python or C/C++; relevant vision, graphics or machine-learning experience. Rendering or optics experience is desirable.
English languageMeet the host university’s English-language admission rules. An approved alternative or exemption may apply; IELTS is not universally mandatory.

About University of Surrey

University of Surrey is a public research university in Guildford, England. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes across engineering, science, business, health, humanities and social sciences. Its teaching and research connect academic foundations with professional practice, supported by partnerships and work addressing questions in technology, health and contemporary society.

Official website: https://www.surrey.ac.uk/

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 17 January 2027 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

  1. Apply through the Vision, Speech and Signal Processing PhD link in the advert.
  2. Instead of a research proposal, upload a document stating the project title and relevant supervisor.
  3. Complete the programme’s remaining supporting-document requirements.

Application Checklist

  • Document stating the project title and relevant supervisor, uploaded in place of a research proposal
  • Other supporting documents required by the linked PhD programme; consult its current checklist
